industry: Optical Components, Lasers and Photonic Subsystems
thesis: Lumentum has completed its transformation from a cyclical telecom-component supplier into a core AI infrastructure optics vendor. FY2026 revenue rose 83% to $3.01B with non-GAAP operating margin expanding from 9.7% to 29.8%, and Q1 FY2027 guidance of $1.225-1.275B implies roughly 130% year-over-year growth. NVIDIA's March 2026 $2B preferred-stock investment plus a multi-billion purchase commitment hard-codes Lumentum into the AI optics supply chain, and newer lines (optical circuit switches, ultra-high-power CPO lasers, ELS/NPO modules) are only beginning to contribute. The offset is valuation and concentration: the stock is up 467% in twelve months and trades near 43x forward non-GAAP EPS, so the thesis now requires the scale-up to land on schedule.

drivers: Management's stated ~$40 of CY2028 EPS power is achieved, capitalised at 34-40x
Optical circuit switch backlog (well above $400M as of Q2 FY2026) converts and OCS becomes a multi-year, multi-billion product line — Citi frames an ~$11B opportunity shared with Coherent
1.6T cloud-module adoption plus ultra-high-power CPO lasers and ELS/NPO in-rack optics materially expand the addressable TAM
NVIDIA purchase commitment and capacity rights underwrite utilisation of the new U.S. fab, holding non-GAAP operating margin above 40%

base_case.assumptions: FY2027 revenue roughly doubles to the $5B area on the guided Q1 run-rate, non-GAAP operating margin holds near 40%, and FY2027 non-GAAP EPS lands around $19-22 (estimate, derived from the $4.05-4.35 Q1 guide and Street models, not company-guided for the full year). Applying ~50x to that stream brackets the $1,067-1,149 range of published analyst mean targets. Assumes no hyperscaler capex pause and orderly conversion of the remaining $1.6B of convertible notes.

risks: AI optics orders digest after the 2026 pull-forward and the forward multiple compresses toward 20-25x
NVIDIA and hyperscaler concentration cuts the other way — a purchase commitment is not a volume guarantee, and a single roadmap change resets the model
Transceiver ASP erosion and competition from Coherent (also a $2B NVIDIA investee), Innolight, Eoptolink and Applied Optoelectronics compress the 50% gross margin
Execution risk on the U.S. fab and on OCS, UHP laser and CPO yields while capex runs above $150M per quarter
Further dilution: shares outstanding went from 69.8M to 88.6M common plus 2.9M preferred in one year, with $1.6B of converts still in current liabilities

catalysts.event: Q1 FY2027 results — guided to $1.225-1.275B revenue, 39.5-40.5% non-GAAP operating margin and $4.05-4.35 non-GAAP diluted EPS; the first test of the accelerated target model
Bulk of the optical circuit switch backlog ships, converting the stated $400M-plus OCS order book into recognised revenue
1.6T cloud transceiver ramp plus first volume ELS module and NPO engagements — the in-rack optics TAM expansion management flagged on the Q4 call
New U.S. fab build-out funded by NVIDIA's $2B investment; capacity milestones and associated capex cadence
Settlement or equitization of the remaining ~$1.6B of convertible notes now sitting in current liabilities — determines final share count
Management's ~$40 EPS power target for 2028, first articulated at the Deutsche Bank technology conference in late August 2026

key_risks: Valuation: ~43x forward non-GAAP EPS after a 467% twelve-month move, with the price 26% above the 200-day moving average — any guidance wobble de-rates hard
Customer concentration in NVIDIA and a short list of hyperscalers; the multi-billion purchase commitment does not guarantee delivered volumes
AI capex cyclicality — optics orders have historically been the first line item cut when data center spending pauses
Competitive pressure and ASP erosion from Coherent, Innolight, Eoptolink and Applied Optoelectronics in transceivers
Execution and yield risk on OCS, ultra-high-power CPO lasers and the new U.S. fab while capex runs above $150M per quarter
Dilution from convertible equitization and the NVIDIA preferred; $1.6B of converts remain in current liabilities
GAAP optics: the $7.8B non-cash debt-extinguishment charge leaves a $7.8B accumulated deficit and makes GAAP screens unusable
Persistent insider selling through the rally, including the President of Global Business Units and the General Counsel, albeit under Rule 10b5-1 plans
